submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a retrospective detector for procedural or instructional text: it is active in source code, in step-by-step instructions (how-tos, UI navigation, recipes) and in manual or specification sentences that say what to do or what a system does, and it is near-silent (below 0.1 x max) in prose that narrates people and events - fiction, news, and legal or contract writing; the same content roughly doubles when it is phrased as an imperative rather than a third-person declarative. adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Installing the monitoring agent

The agent ships as a single binary and runs as a background service. Before you begin, confirm that the host has at least 2 GB of free disk space and that outbound traffic to port 443 is permitted.

Download the package for your architecture from the release page, verify its checksum against the published manifest, and unpack it into /opt/monitor.

Create a service account for the daemon so that it does not run as root:

  sudo useradd --system --no-create-home monitor

Copy the sample configuration into place and open it in your editor. Set the api_key field to the token issued by the control plane, set the region field to the code nearest your data centre, and leave every other value at its default.

The agent writes its log to /var/log/monitor/agent.log and rotates it at midnight. If the log directory does not exist, create it and give ownership to the service account.

Open port 8443 in the host firewall and allow traffic only from the control plane's address range. Reload the firewall rules and confirm that the rule appears in the list:

  sudo firewall-cmd --reload
  sudo firewall-cmd --list-all

Start the service and check that it reached the running state:

  sudo systemctl enable --now monitor
  sudo systemctl status monitor

Then confirm that the host appears in the fleet view of the dashboard. It can take up to five minutes for the first heartbeat to register, so wait before you assume something is broken.

If the host does not appear, inspect the last fifty lines of the log for authentication errors. A common cause is a clock skew greater than thirty seconds, which the control plane rejects; synchronise the system clock and restart the agent. If the log shows a certificate error instead, re-download the package and check that the checksum matches the value printed on the release page.

Verify the installation from the command line by asking the agent for its version and its configured region:

  monitor --version
  monitor status

Both commands should exit with status zero. A non-zero exit code means the binary is not readable by the service account, so check the file permissions and try again.

To upgrade later, stop the service, replace the binary and start it again. The configuration file is preserved across upgrades, so your settings do not need to be entered a second time.

The agent sends metrics every fifteen seconds and a full inventory snapshot once an hour. Metrics are buffered on disk for up to six hours when the control plane is unreachable, so short network interruptions do not lose data. Each buffered batch is compressed before it is written, and the buffer is trimmed oldest-first once it exceeds 200 MB.

To remove the agent, stop and disable the service, delete the service account and remove /opt/monitor and /var/log/monitor. The control plane drops a host from the fleet view automatically after seven days without a heartbeat.
